Build an interactive slide deck from str: Build an interactive slide deck from structured slides: the agent picks a controlled layout per slide (title, section, agenda, content, dashboard, roadmap, takeaways, closing) composed of typed blocks, native interactive charts included, and the deck renders in chat with keyboard, touch and fullscreen navigation, speaker notes and PDF export. The agent authors structured JSON, never HTML: every human-readable string is flat inline markup rendered through a tokenizer, never an HTML sink. Once a deck exists, edit_presentation changes it surgically (one slide, one block, one word), with every other slide guaranteed byte-identical; calling generate_presentation again with the presentation_id rewrites the same deck wholesale.
Find a reusable design template (present: Find a reusable design template (presentation deck, report, dashboard) by its structured metadata (name, kind, tag, theme, aspect ratio) and read back its layout definitions, theme configuration and asset references (fonts, images, logos). This is an exact metadata filter, not a semantic/RAG search: it never touches a knowledge base, and template content is never embedded or vectorized. Templates are managed via the Template Containers API.
Author a reusable design template from a: Author a reusable design template from a conversation: create a container with a brand palette and a layout catalog, refine it across turns, and bind a file the user already uploaded as its logo, font or background. The write half of Template Search, on its own toggle. Guardrailed against the two ways a template silently does nothing: only theme keys the renderer honours are accepted, and every layout id must really exist. Templates authored here are private to the user (publishing one org-wide stays a human action in the Templates UI), and built-in templates are refused rather than edited, since they are rewritten from code on every deployment.
Look at a source document instead of onl: Look at a source document instead of only reading its extracted words. Renders the pages of a PDF as images the agent sees natively (the one way it can judge a design it is asked to reproduce), reads the EXACT theme of a PowerPoint (colour scheme, heading and body typefaces, slide size) out of the file's own theme part rather than estimating it off a screenshot, and can lift the embedded logos out as platform files. An HTML page is read the same way, statically: its CSS custom properties, the colours and font stacks it declares, and its heading outline, with nothing fetched (an external stylesheet, an @import, an image or a url() is listed, never followed) and nothing executed, so an uploaded page cannot make the backend issue requests on its behalf. Also measures the perceptual distance (ΔE) between a template's palette and the colours it is meant to match, because looking at two renders does not tell anyone #0b1020 from #0c1122.
